blocks.text: Thank you, Stephanie. And I believe we're speaking on 17-25, correct? Okay, very good. So 17-25 is an ordinance that starts a process. The process that this ordinance starts is a process that will culminate if all of the steps are taken with an exemption on real property called a TIF exemption. That TIF exemption would relate to residentially taxed real property. So think of single family homes. This is different than commercial properties where we have logistics facilities or manufacturing. There's a whole different code section that deals with the commercial stuff. Here we're focused on the single family. And because single family involves residents and people who live in homes, the General Assembly treats that area in a special way. The General Assembly does a few things. It requires a little bit more process. It requires eventually a hearing by this council to establish an agreement. It requires some notifications to property owners that are in the surrounding area. So the General Assembly is kind of, you know, doing these things because of just the higher level of scrutiny associated with residential property. Also underneath these laws, the TIF statutes allow for certain property tax millage to go into an infrastructure bucket. not all millage goes there when it's residential because the county has a number of social service levy agencies that need some money for some of those social service needs so the statutes again are very different than in the commercial world where we might have bigger exemptions or broader exemptions for more narrowly tailored in the residential area this specific ordinance what it does is it it focuses in on the powers run area this will be developed by a development group called four star and what they're doing is they're essentially looking at their development plan and they're saying we have multiple phases of development that will come forward an inefficient result when you're doing economic planning would be let's just do everything all at once but the problem with that in the home building world is that all those homes all those lots won't be built in the same year they might be built over two or two and a half or three years and so phasing is typically how a residential home builder deals with that reality similarly on the economic side we want to do the same thing for the city's exemption it will provide the closest tracking to the home building activity so this legislation calls out five different and incentive districts, because we're trying to track the five different growth areas within that subdivision. It's, again, the most efficient way to deal with creating this type of exemption. So those are the kind of key points. There is a, again, a couple other elements that are in this specific preliminary legislation. An economic development plan is in the legislation. That's specific to this residential development area. Again, that's an element of the law. Basically, the General Assembly wants communities like you all to declare that there is insufficient infrastructure in that area. And if you think about it, in order to house that many homes, we would need some roads, we would need some internal improvements. And with no roads present, it's a pretty straightforward conclusion that we don't have the necessary infrastructure in that specific area. This isn't a decision about the city wide. It's really just about that specific area. And then finally, like I said, there are elements of this process. A hearing needs to be scheduled for a little later on. The way that the General Assembly likes to, you know, put these requirements into the community's hands, they would like you all to hear from the residents prior to an exemption. Of course you would do so. Of course you have multiple readings of legislation. The General Assembly is just asking you to have a specific hearing on these exemptions a little bit later on in the process. Following this piece of legislation, it really needs to go into effect for us to do the second thing, which is actually establish the exemption on the ground. There's a lot of process with these types of exemptions. Essentially, General Assembly is putting in place a policy that says, you need to be telling everybody, you should be telling the schools and telling the county and telling the affected property owners that there's a residential exemption that's coming. That's good government, and it's also explaining to everybody what's coming and when. Once all those notices go, then city council has the authorization to actually file an exemption and authorize an exemption. So this legislation doesn't do step two, it just does step one. It kind of lays the framework and follows the statutes so that then you can do step two a little on down the road which is adopt those exemptions so that's thumbnail sketch of what we have in front of us but i'm happy to answer any questions about this or if there's development questions we can certainly speak with miss moscow questions from
